author: Gonçalves et al. (2023)
title: Social gaming: A systematic review
definition: Sociality can be located in co-play, design intent, interactions, outcomes, or the cultural nature of gaming.
setting: Review of gaming literature; not one intervention.
operationalization: Five perspectives: non-solitary; social intent in design; social interactions; social outcomes; sociality inherent to gaming.
outcomes: Social closeness and social capital appear as potential outcomes, not universal participation criteria.
notes: Use as a conceptual map, not as a single empirical operational definition.

author: Kaye (2021)
title: Understanding the “social” nature of digital games
definition: Social experience varies by type of presence and behavioral interdependence.
setting: Digital games, physical and virtual settings.
operationalization: 2 x 2 taxonomy: physical vs. virtual presence crossed with high vs. low task interdependence.
outcomes: Social presence is a related construct.
notes: A taxonomy of dimensions, not a single behavioral measurement protocol.

author: Janssen et al. (2023)
title: A digital gaming intervention to strengthen the social networks of older Dutch adults
definition: Asynchronous game-based exchanges can facilitate meaningful contact across generations.
setting: SamenSpelen mobile group-chat games with older and younger participants.
operationalization: Participation in text/photo-based games; exchange of messages, emoticons, photos, and personal memories prompted by a chatbot.
outcomes: Loneliness and social network strength are outcomes; app engagement may be a process measure.
notes: Chatbot facilitates human-human interaction; it is not necessarily an AI co-player.

author: Iizuka et al. (2019)
title: Does social interaction influence the effect of cognitive intervention program? A randomized controlled trial using Go game
definition: Social interaction is face-to-face group learning and play.
setting: Go lessons and play versus individual computer/tablet Go.
operationalization: Human contact, tactical discussion, questions, nonverbal cues, and post-game feedback; contrast with solo computer condition.
outcomes: Cognitive test performance is an outcome.
notes: The human-versus-computer condition is a manipulation; not every listed behavior was necessarily quantified separately.

author: Miltiades & Thatcher (2017/2019)
title: Social engagement during game play in persons with Alzheimer’s disease
definition: Engagement includes physical, verbal, and emotional responses related to play.
setting: Small-group tabletop tile/puzzle games among people with dementia.
operationalization: Game-related comments, prompting turns, rule reminders, helping others, conversation, laughter, and celebration.
outcomes: Social engagement is the focal observed behavior; other clinical outcomes should be distinguished.
notes: Confirm publication year and exact coding instrument in the primary paper.

author: Maheux et al. (2025)
title: Adolescent social gaming as a form of social media
definition: Digital gameplay with online interaction with others.
setting: Online multiplayer, parallel co-presence, avatars and metagaming communities.
operationalization: Online reciprocal interaction, shared activities, synchronous/asynchronous play, customization, Discord/Twitch-related activity.
outcomes: Peer relationship quality may be an outcome or correlate.
notes: A conceptual perspective; listed affordances are not necessarily all measures used in one empirical study.

author: Benjamini et al. (2025)
title: Connecting screens: the effect of online playful interactions
definition: Distinguishes rule-based social play from spontaneous, reciprocal social playfulness.
operationalization: Spontaneity, reciprocal co-creation, gestures and vocal/facial expression in brief playful interactions.
notes: Playfulness is adjacent to gaming, not interchangeable with structured games.

author: Liu, Li, & Cai (2026)
title: The effects of video games on cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: a meta-analysis
definition: Defines video games broadly as electronic games; social interaction is not central to the supplied description.
operationalization: Motor-cognitive tasks, reaction time, movement and balance; no clear direct social-gaming indicator in supplied summary.
notes: Retain as contextual gaming literature, not a direct operationalization of social gaming.
